basis: The Senate report r23-765 states that the Centre des monuments nationaux manages the villa, gives its mix of civil servants and contract staff, and calls it an administrative public body, while Code du patrimoine articles L141-1 and R141-1 to R141-14 give its board's budget vote and the ministerial approval of loans.

The organisation page says a foundation with its own board runs the studio-house as a non-profit institution with public benefit status, and the 2025 to 2028 policy plan names it Stichting Het Van Doesburghuis.

The press kit states the City of Nancy owns the villa and entrusted its project to the Musée de l'École de Nancy, whose own site is published as Ville de Nancy and describes the collection as municipal heritage.

The foundation's history page says Le Corbusier bequeathed his estate to it and that a decree of 1968 recognised it as a public utility, the visit page shows the foundation opens the apartment, and the Journal Officiel accounts notice calls it a recognised public utility foundation.

governance.parent: Centre des monuments nationaux, under the Ministry of Culture
controls: approval of programme, loans or disposals by a ministry or council

basis: The 2021 press release says the Centre des monuments nationaux manages the site owned by the Conservatoire du littoral, the Senate report r23-765 confirms it and gives the staff mix, and Code du patrimoine articles L141-1 and R141-1 to R141-14 give the centre's status, budget vote and ministerial approvals.

The museum's architecture page says Georg Kolbe's will of 1943 passed his studio house to the Georg Kolbe-Stiftung, its museum page says the foundation was set up in 1950 for his estate, and its team page lists the foundation board and a Kuratorium.
The imprint of the Kunstsammlungen Chemnitz says they are an institution of the City of Chemnitz, and their collections site lists the Henry van de Velde Museum in Villa Esche among their houses.

The imprint names the Ungers Archiv a Stiftung Bürgerlichen Rechts, its foundation page calls it an independent institution built on the Ungers library and estate, and the repairs page dates it to 1990.

The statutes of 7 June 2018 (archived copy of the society's own page) make the ernst-may-gesellschaft a registered Verein that runs the model house and whose members' assembly elects the board, and its society page calls it a non-profit Verein.
The City of Hagen's page for its Fachbereich Museen und Archive says the department looks after the Hohenhof and the Osthaus Museum.
